title: Migration 41 — effective-dated rulesets
description: Applies migration 39, 40 then 41, runs 41's VERIFY A-G, then rolls back 41 on a disposable PostgreSQL 18 cluster. compliance_rules already had jurisdiction, severity, is_blocking and an approval lifecycle; what it had no concept of was TIME. The platform could answer 'is this compliant today' but not 'was this compliant when it left', which is the only question anyone asks after the fact -- and Thai cannabis regulation changed materially three times in four years. 41 adds effective_from/effective_to to compliance_rules, a versioned destination_rulesets table, and the two point-in-time resolvers that are the only supported way to ask what applied on a given day. The backfill (effective_from = created_at) is an ASSUMPTION and every backfilled row is flagged effective_from_is_estimated, because a rule transcribed later than it took effect will otherwise be under-applied to historic shipments and nobody would be able to tell which dates were guesses.

verify.note: C is the section that matters and it asserts BOTH directions: a rule effective in 30 days is not in force today, AND a rule closed 30 days ago IS still in force at a date inside its own window -- the second is what makes judging a March shipment by March's rules possible, and a naive 'status = active' filter passes the first test while failing the second. C also pins the boundary semantics (effective_from inclusive, effective_to exclusive) and proves status still gates inside the window. F asserts that an unresearched market returns NO ROW; the export gate must read that as unresolved and refuse, because an empty result is not permission. Migration 41's one-current-ruleset guarantee is an INDEX (race-free); the closed-range overlap check is a TRIGGER and is NOT race-free -- that limitation is stated in the migration header rather than hidden, and closing it needs btree_gist.
